newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Citicorp joins Brazil CVRD bidders.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp joins Brazil CVRD bidders.

text.p: Citicorp will be bidding in the privatizaton auction of Brazilian mining giant CVRD as a member of an investment fund created specifically for this purpose, said a spokesman for one of the two consortia planning to bid in the auction.
"Citibank has joined our consortium," said Francisco Padilha, spokesman for Brazilian steelmaker CSN, which is leading the Valepar consortium. "It's investing in the Opportunity fund."
Brazil's Opportunity Asset Management, a member of Valepar, set up the offshore Sweet River fund for foreign, mainly U.S., investors interested in investing in the privatization of CVRD.

Newspaper reports said Citibank was planning to place at least $300 million in the Sweet River fund, but was willing to up that amount to almost double should the bidding for CVRD get really fierce. Neither Citibank, nor CSN, nor Opportunity would confirm these figures.

U.S. billionaire investor George Soros is also participating in Opportunity's investment fund, according to CSN Chairman Benjamin Steinbruch, but the size of the tycoon's investment has not been revealed.

The auction of a 45 percent voting stake in CVRD was scheduled to take place April 29, but a flood of lawsuits against the privatization has managed to halt the selloff until further court action decides the validity of the legal challenges.
Valepar's rival is the Valecom consortium led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
